data.description:
## Problem

`Mirror Guard` fails spuriously whenever a Gerrit change is submitted while a guard
run is in flight. The run reports the invariant failure

```
Gerrit/GitHub main diverged or Gerrit MERGED revisions are not reachable from main.
```

even though replication is healthy and self-corrects within seconds.

## Evidence

Run `35497408797` (2026-09-20):

- Run started `07:38`, error logged `2026-09-20T07:41:58.1712866Z`.
- Gerrit change **2997** (`Preserve partial metered Bedrock spend`, revision
  `1f338f2c57e`) was submitted at **07:41:48** — **10 seconds before** the error.
- The next scheduled run at `07:49` passed with no intervention, as did `08:21`,
  `08:41` and `08:50`.

The first hypothesis — that changes 2998/2999 caused it — is refuted: both were
submitted at `08:08:53`, 27 minutes *after* the failure.

## Root cause

Two compounding defects in `src/rebar/mirror_guard.py`, both in how
`merged_reachability_check` differs from the replication check beside it.

**1. No lag tolerance.** `_replication_check_with_lag_tolerance`
(`src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:305`) re-samples up to 3 times, 45s apart, explicitly to
absorb replication lag. `merged_reachability_check` (`src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:253`)
is called once from `run()` (`src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:378-379`) with no re-sample and
no tolerance of any kind. The workflow header in
`.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml` advertises the ~45s window as if it covered the
whole job; it covers only the replication half.

**2. The comparison baseline is a stale snapshot.** `merged_reachability_check` proves
each merged revision is an ancestor of `destination_ref`, which defaults to `"HEAD"`.
In the workflow, `HEAD` is the `actions/checkout` of GitHub `main` taken at job start.
So the guard compares Gerrit's *live* MERGED list against a GitHub `main` snapshot
captured minutes earlier. The race window is therefore the job's own runtime — about
3 minutes in run `35497408797` — not the ~15s replication lag the design anticipated.

Any submit landing inside that window is guaranteed to appear unreachable.

## Why it matters

Mirror Guard exists to detect a genuinely broken mirror lock. It runs every 15
minutes. A false positive on every merge that races a run destroys exactly the signal
the guard is for, and trains readers to ignore it — the same failure mode as the
alarm-quality bugs already tracked in this store.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `merged_reachability_check` re-fetches the GitHub `main` tip rather than comparing against the checkout-time `HEAD`.
- [ ] A merged revision that is unreachable on the first sample is re-sampled before the run fails.
- [ ] A revision that becomes reachable during the re-sample window yields a healthy verdict.
- [ ] A revision that stays unreachable across the whole window still yields an unhealthy verdict.
- [ ] The healthy-after-re-sample verdict states in its `reason` that it converged, matching the replication check's existing wording.
- [ ] The re-sample count and delay are shared with the replication check rather than duplicated as separate literals.
- [ ] The `.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml` header no longer implies the re-sample window covers a check that does not re-sample.
- [ ] A unit test reproduces run `35497408797`: a revision submitted after checkout, unreachable on sample 1, reachable on sample 2, producing a healthy verdict.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports no new or increased entries.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports no new entries.

## Verification

```
pytest tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py -v
```

must exit zero with every test passing; each behavioural criterion above has a named
test there. Repository gates are proven by `make lint` and `make typecheck`, each
exiting zero.
data.title: Mirror Guard's merged-reachability check has no lag tolerance, so any merge during a run reds it
